title.es: La estructura causativa (have / get something done)

text.en: The causative says that someone else does something for us, or that something happens to us. The structure is have/get + object + participle (“I had my car repaired.”). Spanish uses “mandé arreglar mi carro” or “me arreglaron el carro” for this. The English “I repaired my car”, however, means I fixed it myself.
text.es: La estructura causativa dice que otra persona hace algo por nosotros, o que algo nos sucede. Su estructura es have/get + objeto + participio («I had my car repaired.»). El español usa para esto «mandé arreglar mi carro» o «me arreglaron el carro». En cambio, el inglés «I repaired my car» significa que lo arreglé yo mismo.

rows: la palabra informal parecida a have

text.en: The participle says what happens to the object: it gets repaired, cut, painted. Get is more casual than have.
text.es: El participio dice lo que le pasa al objeto: lo arreglan, lo cortan, lo pintan. Get es más informal que have.

examples.es: I had my car repaired last week.

tr.en: I had my car repaired last week.
tr.es: La semana pasada mandé arreglar mi carro.

examples.es: She is getting her hair cut tomorrow.

tr.en: She is getting her hair cut tomorrow.
tr.es: Mañana le van a cortar el pelo.

text.en: Work done by yourself uses the simple verb: “I cut my hair” (I cut it), “I had my hair cut” (someone cut it).
text.es: El trabajo hecho por uno mismo usa el verbo simple: «I cut my hair» (yo me lo corté), «I had my hair cut» (me lo cortaron).

tr.en: I cut my hair myself.
tr.es: Yo mismo me corté el pelo.

examples.es: I had my hair cut at the salon.

tr.en: I had my hair cut at the salon.
tr.es: Me cortaron el pelo en la peluquería.

title.en: An unpleasant event: have + object + participle
title.es: Un suceso desagradable: have + objeto + participio

text.en: The same structure also says that something bad happened to us. We did not ask for it or want it.
text.es: La misma estructura también dice que nos pasó algo malo. No lo pedimos ni lo quisimos.

examples.es: He had his wallet stolen on the bus.

tr.en: He had his wallet stolen on the bus.
tr.es: Le robaron la cartera en el camión.

examples.es: They had their car damaged in the storm.

tr.en: They had their car damaged in the storm.
tr.es: Su carro se dañó en la tormenta.

title.en: A person as object: have + person + base verb, get + person + to
title.es: Una persona como objeto: have + persona + verbo base, get + persona + to

text.en: If you name who does it, have takes the base verb (without to), and get takes to + base verb.
text.es: Si nombras quién lo hace, have lleva el verbo base (sin to) y get lleva to + verbo base.

examples.es: I had the mechanic check the brakes.

tr.en: I had the mechanic check the brakes.
tr.es: Le pedí al mecánico que revisara los frenos.

examples.es: I got the mechanic to check the brakes.

tr.en: I got the mechanic to check the brakes.
tr.es: Convencí al mecánico de revisar los frenos.

text.en: Have/get changes with every tense, and the participle stays: “I’m having my kitchen painted”, “I’ve had my eyes tested”, “Where do you get your hair cut?”
text.es: Have/get cambia con cada tiempo, y el participio se queda: «I’m having my kitchen painted», «I’ve had my eyes tested», «Where do you get your hair cut?»

examples.es: I'm having my kitchen painted at the moment.

tr.en: I'm having my kitchen painted at the moment.
tr.es: Ahorita me están pintando la cocina.

examples.es: Where do you get your hair cut?

tr.en: Where do you get your hair cut?
tr.es: ¿Dónde te cortas el pelo?

text.en: The participle comes after the object, not before it: not “I had repaired my car”, but “I had my car repaired”. “Had repaired” would be the past perfect: I fixed it myself.
text.es: El participio va después del objeto, no antes: no «I had repaired my car», sino «I had my car repaired». «Had repaired» sería el past perfect: yo mismo lo arreglé.

text.en: Make and let are causative verbs too: “The teacher made us stay” (forced us), “She let me use her phone” (allowed it). After them there is always the base verb, without to.
text.es: Make y let también son verbos causativos: «The teacher made us stay» (nos obligó), «She let me use her phone» (lo permitió). Después de ellos siempre va el verbo base, sin to.

speak.en: The causative says that someone else does something for us. The structure is «have» or «get», then the object, then the participle: «I had my car repaired». If you did it yourself, you use the simple verb: «I repaired my car». For an unpleasant event the same structure is used: «He had his wallet stolen». If you name who does it: «I had the mechanic check the brakes» and «I got the mechanic to check the brakes». After «make» and «let» there is also the base verb.
speak.es: La estructura causativa dice que otra persona hace algo por nosotros. Su estructura es «have» o «get», luego el objeto y luego el participio: «I had my car repaired». Si lo hiciste tú mismo, usas el verbo simple: «I repaired my car». Para un suceso desagradable se usa la misma estructura: «He had his wallet stolen». Si nombras quién lo hace: «I had the mechanic check the brakes» y «I got the mechanic to check the brakes». Después de «make» y «let» también va el verbo base.

items.sentence: I ___ my car repaired last week.

why.en: A service in the past: had + object + participle.
why.es: Un servicio en el pasado: had + objeto + participio.

did.en: “Did my car repaired” does not exist; the causative uses have or get.
did.es: «Did my car repaired» no existe; la estructura causativa usa have o get.

made.en: “Made my car repaired” does not exist; make would take a base verb.
made.es: «Made my car repaired» no existe; make llevaría un verbo base.

tr.en: I had my car repaired last week.
tr.es: Mandé reparar mi carro la semana pasada.

items.sentence: She is getting her hair ___ tomorrow.

why.en: After get + object comes the participle: cut (its form equals the base verb).
why.es: Después de get + objeto va el participio: cut (su forma es igual al verbo base).

to cut.en: Get + object + to cut would mean the hair cuts; you need the participle.
to cut.es: Get + objeto + to cut significaría que el pelo corta; hace falta el participio.

cutting.en: Cutting would mean the hair is cutting; you need the participle.
cutting.es: Cutting significaría que el pelo está cortando; hace falta el participio.

tr.en: She is getting her hair cut tomorrow.
tr.es: Ella se va a cortar el cabello mañana.

items.sentence: We're having the kitchen ___ at the moment.

why.en: A service in progress: having + object + participle.
why.es: Un servicio en marcha: having + objeto + participio.

paint.en: “Having the kitchen paint” is not correct; the kitchen is painted, so you need the participle.
paint.es: «Having the kitchen paint» no es correcto; la cocina es pintada, por eso hace falta el participio.

painting.en: Having the kitchen painting would mean the kitchen paints; you need the participle.
painting.es: Having the kitchen painting significaría que la cocina pinta; hace falta el participio.

examples: I am having my hair cut.
He is having his car washed.

tr.en: We're having the kitchen painted at the moment.
tr.es: Nos están pintando la cocina en este momento.

items.sentence: He had his wallet ___ on the bus.

why.en: An unpleasant event: had + object + participle (stolen).
why.es: Un suceso desagradable: had + objeto + participio (stolen).

stole.en: Stole is the simple past, not the participle; after had his wallet you need the participle (stolen).
stole.es: Stole es el pasado simple, no el participio; después de had his wallet hace falta el participio (stolen).

steal.en: Steal is the base verb; if the person does not act, you need the participle (stolen).
steal.es: Steal es el verbo base; si la persona no actúa, hace falta el participio (stolen).

examples: They had their car broken into.

tr.en: He had his wallet stolen on the bus.
tr.es: Le robaron la cartera en el camión.

items.sentence: I need to ___ my eyes tested.

make.en: “Make my eyes tested” is not correct; make would take a base verb.
make.es: «Make my eyes tested» no es correcto; make llevaría un verbo base.

do.en: “Do my eyes tested” does not exist; a service needs have or get.
do.es: «Do my eyes tested» no existe; un servicio necesita have o get.

examples: I want to have it fixed.

tr.en: I need to have my eyes tested.
tr.es: Necesito que me revisen los ojos.

items.sentence: I had the mechanic ___ the brakes.

why.en: After have + person comes the base verb, without to: had the mechanic check.
why.es: Después de have + persona va el verbo base, sin to: had the mechanic check.

to check.en: After have there is no to; to goes with get (got the mechanic to check).
to check.es: Después de have no va to; to va con get (got the mechanic to check).

checked.en: Had the mechanic checked would be the past perfect; after a person you need the base verb.
checked.es: Had the mechanic checked sería el past perfect; después de una persona hace falta el verbo base.

tr.en: I had the mechanic check the brakes.
tr.es: Hice que el mecánico revisara los frenos.

items.sentence: I got the mechanic ___ the brakes.

why.en: After get + person comes to + base verb: got the mechanic to check.
why.es: Después de get + persona va to + verbo base: got the mechanic to check.

check.en: After get with a person you need to; the base verb without to goes with have.
check.es: Después de get con una persona hace falta to; el verbo base sin to va con have.

checking.en: Here you need to + base verb (get + person + -ing exists, but it means to set something going: get him talking).
checking.es: Aquí hace falta to + verbo base (get + persona + -ing existe, pero significa poner en marcha: get him talking).

tr.en: I got the mechanic to check the brakes.
tr.es: Logré que el mecánico revisara los frenos.

items.sentence: Where do you ___ your hair cut?

why.en: A service in a question: get + object + participle.
why.es: Un servicio en una pregunta: get + objeto + participio.

make.en: “Make your hair cut” is not correct; make would take a base verb.
make.es: «Make your hair cut» no es correcto; make llevaría un verbo base.

do.en: “Do your hair cut” does not exist; a service needs have or get.
do.es: «Do your hair cut» no existe; un servicio necesita have o get.

examples: Where do you get your car washed?
Where did she get it fixed?

tr.en: Where do you get your hair cut?
tr.es: ¿Dónde te cortas el cabello?

items.sentence: Did you cut your hair? No, I ___ it cut.

why.en: Someone else cut it: had + object + participle.
why.es: Otra persona lo cortó: had + objeto + participio.

did.en: “Did it cut” does not exist; the causative uses have or get.
did.es: «Did it cut» no existe; la estructura causativa usa have o get.

was.en: “Was it cut” is not the right order here; you need the structure had it cut.
was.es: «Was it cut» no es el orden correcto aquí; hace falta la estructura had it cut.

tr.en: Did you cut your hair? No, I had it cut.
tr.es: ¿Te cortaste el cabello tú mismo? No, me lo mandé cortar.

items.sentence: He had his car ___ in the storm.

why.en: An unpleasant event: had + object + participle (damaged).
why.es: Un suceso desagradable: had + objeto + participio (damaged).

damage.en: Damage is the base verb; after the object you need the participle (damaged).
damage.es: Damage es el verbo base; después del objeto hace falta el participio (damaged).

to damage.en: After had there is no to + verb; you need the participle (damaged).
to damage.es: Después de had no va to + verbo; hace falta el participio (damaged).

tr.en: He had his car damaged in the storm.
tr.es: Su carro se dañó en la tormenta.

items.sentence: I'll have the documents ___ to you tomorrow.

why.en: Object + participle: the documents will be sent.
why.es: Objeto + participio: los documentos serán enviados.

send.en: Have the documents send would mean the documents send; you need the participle.
send.es: Have the documents send significaría que los documentos envían; hace falta el participio.

sending.en: Have the documents sending would mean the documents are sending; you need the participle.
sending.es: Have the documents sending significaría que los documentos están enviando; hace falta el participio.

tr.en: I'll have the documents sent to you tomorrow.
tr.es: Haré que te envíen los documentos mañana.

items.sentence: He got his brother ___ him with the move.

why.en: After get + person comes to + base verb: got his brother to help.
why.es: Después de get + persona va to + verbo base: got his brother to help.

help.en: After get with a person you need to.
help.es: Después de get con una persona hace falta to.

helped.en: Got his brother helped would mean his brother was helped; after a person you need to + base verb.
helped.es: Got his brother helped significaría que ayudaron a su hermano; después de una persona hace falta to + verbo base.

tr.en: He got his brother to help him with the move.
tr.es: Hizo que su hermano lo ayudara con la mudanza.

items.sentence: Have you ever ___ your eyes tested?

why.en: A service in the present perfect: have you had + object + participle.
why.es: Un servicio en presente perfecto: have you had + objeto + participio.

have.en: “Have you ever have” is not correct; after the present perfect you need the participle of have (had).
have.es: «Have you ever have» no es correcto; después del presente perfecto hace falta el participio de have (had).

making.en: “Have you ever making” is not correct; you need had.
making.es: «Have you ever making» no es correcto; hace falta had.

tr.en: Have you ever had your eyes tested?
tr.es: ¿Alguna vez te han revisado los ojos?

items.sentence: The boss had everyone ___ the form.

why.en: After have + person comes the base verb, without to: had everyone sign.
why.es: Después de have + persona va el verbo base, sin to: had everyone sign.

to sign.en: After have there is no to; to goes with get.
to sign.es: Después de have no va to; to va con get.

signed.en: Had everyone signed would be the past perfect; after a person you need the base verb.
signed.es: Had everyone signed sería el past perfect; después de una persona hace falta el verbo base.

tr.en: The boss had everyone sign the form.
tr.es: El jefe hizo que todos firmaran el formulario.

items.sentence: She got her son ___ his room.

why.en: After get + person comes to + base verb: got her son to clean.
why.es: Después de get + persona va to + verbo base: got her son to clean.

clean.en: After get with a person you need to.
clean.es: Después de get con una persona hace falta to.

cleaning.en: After get with a person comes to + base verb, not an -ing form.
cleaning.es: Después de get con una persona va to + verbo base, no una forma -ing.

tr.en: She got her son to clean his room.
tr.es: Ella logró que su hijo limpiara su cuarto.

items.sentence: I'm going to ___ a new roof put on the house.

do.en: “Do a new roof put” does not exist; a service needs have or get.
do.es: «Do a new roof put» no existe; un servicio necesita have o get.

let.en: Let would take a base verb; here the roof goes with a participle, so you need have.
let.es: Let llevaría un verbo base; aquí el techo va con un participio, por eso hace falta have.

examples: I want to have it painted.

tr.en: I'm going to have a new roof put on the house.
tr.es: Voy a mandar poner un techo nuevo a la casa.

items.sentence: Anna ___ her hair cut every month at the same salon.

why.en: A regular service: has + object + participle.
why.es: Un servicio habitual: has + objeto + participio.

makes.en: “Makes her hair cut” is not correct; make would take a base verb.
makes.es: «Makes her hair cut» no es correcto; make llevaría un verbo base.

does.en: “Does her hair cut” does not exist; a service needs has or gets.
does.es: «Does her hair cut» no existe; un servicio necesita has o gets.

tr.en: Anna has her hair cut every month at the same salon.
tr.es: Anna se corta el cabello cada mes en el mismo salón.
